plain_english: From change, that One is longed for, for all spirits — and yet body's and earth's and the rest's change is by nature.
sanskrit_cite: pariṇāmāttadekaṃ hi sarvānpuṃsaḥ pratīṣyate tathāpi dehabhūtādeḥ pariṇāmaḥ svabhāvataḥ

plain_english: As before — why would it not be, toward the deemed-freed? Yet it does occur — but is not joined by him.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvavanna bhavetkasmāttaṃ muktābhimataṃ prati athāpi sa bhavatyeva kiṃ tu tena na yujyate

plain_english: By the freed spirit — done with tasks, need-free — he stands alone; not so: needlessness belongs to no spirit ever, nor to mind.
sanskrit_cite: muktapuṃsā kṛtārthatvādanarthitvātsa kevalaḥ naitannārthitvamasyāsti jātu puṃso'tha cetasaḥ

plain_english: With need gone, no meeting with spirit again would be; this too is unjust, once body-dwelling mind is born.
sanskrit_cite: arthitvavigamānna syādbhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ tadetadapi na nyāyyaṃ jāte dehasthacetasi

plain_english: If from perceptible-only-nature of that, not from karma's waning — mokṣa would be mere nature, resting on karma's waning.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvedyaikasvabhāvatvāttasya karmakṣayānna cet tatsvabhāvatvameva syānmokṣaḥ karmakṣayāśrayaḥ

plain_english: There'd be acts even of spirit-distinction-knowers, from compassion; if not from passion — thus mokṣa from passion's exhaustion.
sanskrit_cite: syurjñātapuṃvivekānāṃ karmāṇyapi kṛpāditaḥ na rāgāttāni cedevaṃ mokṣo rāgakṣayādbhavet

plain_english: Thus view-abandoned — that nature-view is unjust; hence body-and-rest, famously, have sentient-maker as prior.
sanskrit_cite: tathā ca darśanatyāgastanna yuktā svabhāvadṛk tasmātprasiddhaṃ tanvādi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam

plain_english: This reason, aimed at the Supreme Lord by the self-entrusted self, is not overpowered by reason-faults in the least — nor the rival's either; only this is said.
sanskrit_cite: sa eṣa hetuḥ parameśvaraṃ prati prayujyamānaḥ svaniveśitātmanā na hetudoṣaiḥ paribhūyate manāk paro'pi vā kevalametaducyate
